questions.stem: How does the structure of cellulose make it suitable for its function in plant cell walls?

options.text: It is branched so can store lots of glucose
Straight chains form hydrogen bonds with neighbouring chains, creating strong microfibrils
It is soluble so it can be transported easily
It coils into a helix to save space

questions.explanation: Cellulose chains are straight and form many hydrogen bonds with neighbouring chains. These cross-links create strong microfibrils that provide structural support to plant cell walls.
